The Harbour Bridge will close to all traffic from the second of November for six weeks while engineers replace the steel joints that carry the road deck over its two piers, the city council confirmed on Tuesday.

Inspections in the summer found that two of the joints had cracked, and that water was reaching the bearings beneath them. Engineers say the bridge is safe to use until the work begins, but that the repairs cannot wait for another winter of salt and frost.

Diversions

Drivers will be sent along the ring road to the Wharf Street crossing, which the council expects to add between ten and twenty minutes to journeys at peak times. Temporary traffic lights at the Mill Lane junction will be timed to favour the diversion.

The three bus routes that use the bridge will run on the diversion as well, and the operator has added extra early services so that people who work in the hospital and the port can still arrive for the start of their shifts.

Walking and cycling

A covered walkway will stay open on the eastern side of the bridge for the whole closure, so people on foot and on bicycles can still cross. Cyclists will be asked to dismount at either end, where the contractors will store materials and park their cranes.

The repairs will cost a little under four million pounds, most of it paid by a national fund for ageing bridges. Councillors said the closure was timed to avoid the Christmas shopping season, and that work would continue at night to finish it sooner.
